runs.name: Consolidated Edison, Inc.; NYSE ED, SEC CIK 0001047862, 10-K filer; holding company of Consolidated Edison Company of New York (CECONY) and Orange and Rockland Utilities, rate-regulated electric, gas and steam delivery in New York City, Westchester and nearby areas; the Clean Energy Businesses sold 2023-03-01; forward sale of 7,000,000 shares settled March 2026, an ATM programme of 2026-05-08; the 10-K names no delivery rival, National Grid's New York companies, Avangrid's New York utilities and National Fuel Gas's utility chosen as a CONVENTION of the run
runs.entry: Price **$112.26** (close 2026-10-16, aggregator, flagged). Shares **369,828,633** common on the 10-Q cover as of 2026-07-31 (`Screens/cover_shares.py` agreeing; the walk from 361M checked against the March 2026 forward settlement and the June ATM deliveries; about 0.95M ATM forward shares unsettled, not added); market cap $41,517M. Sovereign **5.43%**, US Treasury 30-year par yield 2026-10-16. Read from the 10-K FY2025 (0001047862-26-000031), the 10-Ks FY2024, FY2023, FY2022 and FY2020, the 10-Q of 2026-06-30 (0001047862-26-000142), the proxy (0001047862-26-000078), the 8-Ks of 2025-11-24 to 2026-09-04 and the Q4 2025 presentation (0001047862-26-000028); lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7, stated in the run file; 2025 operating cash $4,800M and depreciation $2,321M cross-checked to the filed statements; `tools/run.py` window stopping at 2022 (utility capex filed under an element it does not read, cost of removal omitted), owner cash built by hand from the filed statements. **Q1 IN**: a regulated delivery monopoly read through its rate plans, allowed return on equity 9.0%, 8.8%, 9.25% and 9.40% on a 48% equity ratio; the open risks the regulator and the gas network under the state climate law (gas 27% of CECONY's operating income). **Q2 IN**: CECONY decides at 91% of five-year operating profit; the castle is the legal franchise, the 10-K calling another authorized deliverer not "reasonably likely"; earned returns 8% to 9.8%, ordinary, carried to Q3 under the regulator exception. **Q3 UNDECIDED**: a fair regulated return on added capital, a second best; about $5.6B of new shares planned for 2026 to 2030. **Q4 WEIGHS AGAINST, no STOP**: ten balance sheets read (2018, 2019, 2024, 2025 checked to the filed statements); equity up $9.9B and long-term debt up $10.8B together; receivables up 134% against revenue up 40%, explained by CECONY's over-60-day balances of $1,427M against $408M before the pandemic; a $1,059M regulatory asset from the income-tax audit open since 2018, earning no return; regulatory deferrals of $0.5B to $1.2B a year swinging the cash, so five years averaged; the adjusted-figure and guidance habit. **Q5 integrity IN** (the weld-film misconduct by contractors found and disclosed by the company, the tax error disclosed), **ability WEIGHS FOR, narrowly**; the annual incentive on adjusted EPS. **Q6 Part A and Part B WEIGH AGAINST**: the 2023 buyback of $1,000M named a sum, not a price, and paid $94.85 a share, above the whole value range; serial issuance in 2021, 2025 and 2026; the dividend paid while new stock is sold. **Q7 OUT**, equity-only central under Q7, The regulated utility: owner cash **$1,226M a year** equity-only maintenance-only (2021 to 2025, depreciation as the maintenance guess, cost of removal and stock pay deducted), **$187M** after all spending with the debt credited ($8,185M of the Utilities' long-term debt raised net of retirements, under the 52% allowed debt share of $12,138M); value range **$14.35 to $61.04 a share equity-only** (bottom all spending at the 5.43% cap, top maintenance-only no growth), all-equity beside -$123.30 to $28.27; fair price **$20.24 equity-only, central**, -$57.52 all-equity, not positive; the best case returns 2.95% at the price, below the floor and the 5.43% bond; the strongest contrary test (GAAP net income at the company's 6.5% target, shown only to test the close) 7.87%. Q8 to Q12 not reached. After the stop, facts recorded, not weighed: pre-tax interest cover 2.2x to 3.5x over 2020 to 2025; long-term debt $26,843M at 2026-06-30, maturities refinanced, not paid; the parent's dividends limited by the NYSPSC to the Utilities' two-year income. Competitors: none named in the 10-K; the same regulator's other SEC-filing franchises chosen as a CONVENTION (National Grid's New York companies earning 8.5% to 9.0%, Avangrid's New York utilities allowed 8.80% then 9.20%, earned not stated, National Fuel Gas's utility allowed 9.7%), 2017 to 2025. Strongest evidence against: the owners must keep adding money at a fair return and no more; shares sold and bought back above every case of the range; customers paying more slowly. Commits 6d8106c7 (Step 0, foundations, lines of evidence), 6f68f654 (Q1), d66a6254 (Q2), 3903aafa (Q3), 5bc171c5 (Q4), 996956a0 (Q5), d491e1de (Q6), 7ee577c1 (Q7), 349381e5 (box, after the stop, self-audit, gaps); killed at 15:59 by a usage limit after Step 0 and resumed by one analyst in the 16:46 cycle. Position note filled at the fold: not held. Contamination declared: commit subjects of other runs (ELPC, AYI, ARCB) and the ED skip line of the overnight log, memory-index lines, the framework's own sentence on sixteen utilities; none used. Citations: the analyst's `check_ids.py` 0 problems; the dispatcher's `_dispatcher_cite_check.py` no missing id, 54 adjacent quoted fragments, 14 flagged and all read: filing quotes, section headers, an id placed before its own quotation and one framework sentence attributed to the framework beside an id cited for its own point, **no citation slip**. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) Q7, The regulated utility's "long-term debt raised" does not say gross or net of retirements, nor whether parent debt counts; the readings move the bottom from $14.35 to $31.50; (2) whether the debt credit applies to the maintenance-only no-growth case (none given); (3) the cap's two sentences in (f) when the cut rate exceeds the sovereign (5.43% carried); (4) Q2's rival test for a monopoly whose filing names no competitor; (5) Q2's regulator exception sends returns to Q3 and Q3 has no paragraph receiving them. Could not get: Avangrid's earned New York return; O&R's debt retirements (its credit an upper bound, about $120M a year); the Clean Energy Businesses' 2021 and 2022 depreciation not re-read on resume; no maintenance split of capital spending. Armed at the equity-only fair price.
runs.narr: OUT at Q7 (Consolidated Edison, ED; New York City regulated electric, gas and steam delivery; Q1 IN; Q2 IN, CECONY deciding at 91% on the legal franchise, ordinary regulated returns carried to Q3; Q3 UNDECIDED; Q4 WEIGHS AGAINST, receivables and the $1,059M tax-audit asset; Q5 integrity IN, ability narrowly for; Q6 against, a priceless 2023 buyback at $94.85 and serial issuance; owner cash $1,226M a year equity-only maintenance-only, $187M after all spending with $8,185M of debt credited; value range $14.35 to $61.04 equity-only vs $112.26, best case 2.95%; fair $20.24 equity-only, armed (-$57.52 all-equity, not positive); no citation slip; not held; framework gaps for the operator: debt raised gross or net and parent debt in the utility credit, the credit at no growth, the cap's two sentences in (f), the rival test for a monopoly, Q3 receiving Q2's regulator exception)
